page.layout: One column of alphabetical index entries in italic, flush left, running down the page and cut off at the right edge. Two centred lines (one word, one number) sit within the column. No running head, page number, catchword or signature visible.; One column of index lines running down the strip, each line a word or name at the left with its page number at the right. A woodcut ornament sits at the lower part of the strip, below the last line.; One column of index entries at the right, names with page numbers; the left edge carries clipped digits of a cut column; below the entries a printed ornament with the line "D·MEM·".; One column of alphabetical index entries, with page numbers at the right, and a section letter (V, X, Z) before each group. A woodcut ornament sits below the entries. No running head or page number.
page.notes: Entries are cut off at the right edge of the scan, so only their opening letters are visible; they are copied as far as they show. The lines marked "Sibylla" are the same heading repeated, with the rest of each entry cut off. A stray dash stands in the left margin beside one entry and is not printed text. The index lines are fragments at the left edge of this strip and are kept as they stand. The line "Libyca, seu L" runs off the right edge, so the continuation is not shown. The numeral after "amis" is doubtful and is marked [?]. The woodcut ornament at the lower part of the strip is an illustration, not printed text, and is not transcribed. The clipped digits at the far left edge (4, 4, 6, 8, 4, 01, 52, 38, 38, 39, 39, 83, 83, 0, 54, 74, 68, 68, 74, 43) are fragments of page numbers from a column that is cut off, so they are not transcribed as entries. "Amaz" is followed by a mark over the line that I could not resolve; read as "Amaz[?]". The "X." beside INDEX at the head is not included in the running head. No page number is visible in this part. The numerals in the Tullia and Vergilius lines are printed with a broken or spaced digit and are uncertain. The page numbers in the Acharias and Zaleucus lines are clear. The first entry is at the top of the scan, so this part starts mid-index.
